newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. farm head attacks Greenpeace corn gene action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm head attacks Greenpeace corn gene action.

text.p: American Farm Bureau Federation president Dean Kleckner on Tuesday attacked environmental group Greenpeace's campaign against U.S. exports of gene-altered soybeans and corn.

"They're (Greenpeace) just publicity seeking to raise more money for their campaigns and their arguments are not based on science," Kleckner told Reuters on the sidelines of the World Trade Organization (WTO) ministerial conference in Singapore.
Greenpeace said in Hamburg on Monday that it was planning to sue importers, shipowners and authorities which allowed U.S. gene-modified corn into the European Union (EU) in breach of current rules.
The group said that too little is known about possible environmental effects of the new strain and a "marker gene" used in the new corn could lower antibiotic resistance in humans and animals.
"It (gene modification) is just like getting your child vaccinated against a disease, it makes sense and will raise yields," Kleckner said.
The EU Commission is due to decide on December 18 whether to allow imports of such modified corn, made by Swiss chemicals company Ciba Geigy AG CIGZsn.S.
Until then, it is illegal to market it in the EU, but Greenpeace says shipments of the new corn may already have arrived in Germany, Italy and the Netherlands.
